top_items.title: Warren Buffett’s Berkshire Just Hit a Record High as Nvidia Sank. A 67-Year-Old Who Bought 1,000 Shares in 2016 Can Sell $106,000 of It This Year and Pay 0% on the Gain
top_items.summary: Berkshire Hathaway rose all five days and closed Friday at a record $592.94, up 3.9% in the week Nvidia lost its CEO and fell 12.7%. A 67-year-old who bought 1,000 Class B shares ten years ago at $157.93 holds $592,940 and a $435,010 gain in a stock that pays no dividend. Under 2026's 0% capital gains ceiling he can sell 179 shares, about $106,000, and owe nothing on the gain; the only cost is $2,075 of tax on Social Security that the sale makes taxable.
